purpose: Which attention kernel implementations could serve the attention set, as A-tier answers, B-tier expert dispatch, or expert references. This record annotates the upstream source archive; it does not duplicate it.

source_archive.merge_status: Not merged. The archive sits on its own branch and is absent from main, which is all that is known; whether to merge it is an open decision. An earlier version of this record asserted a reason (that .gitignore's vendored-source convention ruled the merge out) and that reason was never agreed with anyone -- it is removed rather than replaced with another guess.
source_archive.consequence: Every upstream fact below is transcribed from that archive's manifest.csv and research_notes.md at the commit above, not researched independently. Re-check against the archive before relying on it; the archive's own verifier covers hash and layout integrity, this record only covers which entry can serve which task.

correction_note: An earlier version of this record claimed the fused attention path was an S5000-only story, on the strength of MATE, MT-flashMLA and MUTLASS each targeting mp_31. That was wrong, and the archive is what shows it: llama.cpp compiles the generic ggml fattn templates for mp_21, mp_22 and mp_31, TileLang-MUSA's deprecated snapshot claims S4000 alongside S5000 and M1000, and torch_musa ships a flash SDP path whose limits are documented. What survives is narrower and more useful: no candidate is a MooreThreads hand-written S4000 attention kernel, and MATE — the library the B-tier contract's argument list matches field for field — requires S5000.

candidates.name: MATE (MUSA AI Tensor Engine)

limits.alignment: fp16/bf16 head dim divisible by 2 without qv, by 8 with qv
limits.layout: BSHD, while this set's B-tier task is BHSD

candidates.why_it_matters: The only candidate that is a maintained, centralized fused attention library, and its argument list maps onto this set's B-tier task contract almost field for field: window_size with -1 for unbounded, causal, softmax_scale, return_softmax_lse, pack_gqa. It also requires S5000, which is the fact that constrains the B-tier task. v0.2.5 is archived alongside it for version comparison.

candidates.name: MT-flashMLA

limits.scope: decoding only, not a general forward attention kernel

candidates.why_it_matters: Moore Threads' counterpart to DeepSeek's FlashMLA, and independent of MATE, so it is a second opinion on any mp_31 attention result. It serves no entry in this set: every entry is forward attention and this is decode.

candidates.name: MUTLASS

requirements.note: README marks these paths as WarpSpecialized

limits.usability: source only; individual .mu files depend on sibling headers, build configuration and a matching MUSA SDK
limits.v0.2.0_note: the earlier revision carries the early MP31 FA forward

candidates.why_it_matters: This is the source a maintainer reads when writing an mp_31 expert dispatch or A-tier kernel, not something to call at runtime. It is also the pinned dependency of MATE and MT-flashMLA, so it explains where their kernels come from.

candidates.name: torch_musa SDPA and the muDNN FlashAttention integration

requirements.note: the only archived candidate that is not pinned to MP31

limits.head_dim: the archive's research notes record that the public SDPA code separates math and flash modes and that the flash path covers only some head dimensions and half precision
limits.backward: not supported in the archived version, so this is not a training path
limits.selection: the submission reaches this through the framework op, so it cannot tell which kernel answered

candidates.why_it_matters: This is the route the B-tier SDPA task assumes for its fused_library path, and the reason the earlier S5000-only claim was wrong. The archive answers part of what was an open question here: a flash path exists but is bounded by head dimension and dtype, which is exactly the kind of boundary a dispatch decision is supposed to discover. Whether any given shape in this set falls inside that boundary is still a measurement, and it is the first thing probe_sdpa.py should settle on the real machine.

candidates.name: llama.cpp ggml FlashAttention templates

requirements.note: ggml-musa/CMakeLists.txt compiles the generic ggml-cuda fattn templates for these targets

limits.provenance: a portable backend path, not a Moore Threads hand-written kernel, so its performance is not evidence about native MUSA attention quality
limits.scope: F16 KV templates with a matrix of ncols1/ncols2 instantiations

candidates.why_it_matters: This is the candidate that breaks the S5000-only claim: it is the one archived implementation whose build files name mp_22 explicitly. It is also the least integrated with this repository's framework, so serving a KernelBench entry from it would take real work. Recorded as the counterexample that keeps the correction honest.

candidates.name: TileLang-MUSA, deprecated final snapshot

requirements.note: upstream lists the tested devices; this repository has not repeated the experiment

limits.status: the upstream repository declared end of maintenance and moved to tile-ai/tilelang-musa, archived separately
limits.type: DSL examples, so the kernels are generated rather than hand-written .mu

candidates.why_it_matters: The second counterexample to the S5000-only claim, and the only archived source that names S4000 and covers backward. Its status word is the honest one: upstream claims tested devices, nobody here repeated it.

candidates.name: TileLang-MUSA, maintained successor

limits.broadest_coverage: the widest attention variant list of any archived candidate

candidates.why_it_matters: Archived separately from the deprecated snapshot rather than overwriting it, because the two have different hardware claims and coverage. If an A-tier kernel is going to be written from a DSL rather than by hand, this is the starting point.

candidates.name: vLLM-MUSA serving kernels

limits.not_all_independent: the archive records that the ordinary FA and MLA calls here are MATE integrations; only the csrc/musa/attention kernels are archived as independent work

candidates.why_it_matters: The largest concentration of real .mu attention source in the archive, including a 1356-line indexer_topk. None of it is forward SDPA, so it serves no entry here, but it is the best available evidence of what Moore Threads' own engineers write when the target is a production serving kernel.

candidates.name: Paddle-MUSA FlashAttention backend

limits.role: a framework registration layer over muDNN and MATE rather than an independent kernel

candidates.why_it_matters: Third independent framework that landed MUSA attention, and the only one besides MATE that covers backward. It confirms the S5000 concentration without adding a new kernel family.

candidates.name: The hand-written MUSA attention kernels already in this repository
coverage: flash-tile band with shared K/V streaming (43/44/50)
two-stage register-tiled SGEMM plus global row softmax (31/97)
one CTA per (window, head) whole-window staging (30)

limits.warp_size_sensitivity: tuned at 128-thread warps with the optimum at the 1024-thread CTA ceiling; not transferable to mp_31 at 32-thread warps without re-measuring
limits.shared_memory: launch configurations are valid only for the head_dim they were measured on

candidates.why_it_matters: The only attention kernels in hand that have actually run on the machine available. They are this set's A-tier answers and the naive-side data the B-tier admission gate needs. They are not candidates for any S5000 fused path.

candidates.name: The framework's own flash attention few-shot example
candidates.role: in-repo reference kernel shown to models
coverage: tiled flash attention with shared Q/K/V staging and running max and sum

requirements.note: CUDA source compiled through torch cpp_extension, so on MUSA it depends on the CUDA-compatible header path or torchada

limits.role: a prompt example, not a benchmarked kernel; it exists to show the submission format

candidates.why_it_matters: Relevant because the model under test has already been shown this kernel. Any A-tier answer for an attention entry overlaps with it, which is worth knowing when judging whether a submission is the model's own work or a remembered template. Added after the earlier version of this record missed it.

archive_entries_not_carried_over.note: The archive lists 13 manifest rows across 9 projects. Every one is represented above except the MATE and MUTLASS duplicate revisions, which are archived for version comparison under the same candidate ids.
registered_but_not_archived: torchada (redirects to MATE and torch_musa flash_attn_interface)
excluded_by_the_archive: Gitee teaching forks whose provenance chain does not close
non-MUSA implementations of the same algorithms
binary-only releases with no public source
MusaCoder, which generates kernels rather than being a fixed-version attention library

gaps: No candidate is a Moore Threads hand-written S4000 attention kernel. The mp_22 paths that exist are a portable ggml template build and a deprecated DSL snapshot whose tested devices are upstream's claim, not a local measurement.

Whether any shape in this set falls inside the torch_musa flash path's head-dimension and dtype window is unmeasured. That is the decisive question for the B-tier task's fused_library expectation on S4000, and probe_sdpa.py should answer it first.
Nothing in this record has been built or run. Every field is transcribed from the archive's manifest and research notes, which themselves record provenance rather than performance.
